parameters.name: table_or_column
parameters.description: If a table is provided, all filters on that table are removed. If a column is provided, only that column's filter is removed. If omitted, all filters on all tables are removed.
parameters.examNote: ALL(Sales) removes all filters on the Sales table. ALL(Sales[Region]) removes only the Region filter, leaving other filters active.

returnType: Table (all rows of the specified table or column, ignoring current filters)
summary: ALL removes filters from a table or specific column. When used inside CALCULATE, it overrides slicer and visual filters to compute totals, percentages, or rank denominators.

examples.label: Percentage of grand total
examples.expression:
% of Total =
DIVIDE(
  SUM(Sales[Amount]),
  CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount]), ALL(Sales))
)
examples.explanation: Numerator = 600 (East only). Denominator uses ALL(Sales) = 1200 (entire table). Result: 600/1200 = 50%.

steps: Current filter context has Region = East (from slicer)
ALL(Sales) removes every active filter on the Sales table
The denominator expression now evaluates across all rows
Result: grand total regardless of slicer selection

commonTraps: ALL() used outside CALCULATE returns a table — it cannot stand alone as a measure value.
ALL(Sales[Region]) removes only the Region filter — other column filters on Sales remain active.
REMOVEFILTERS is the preferred choice when intent is purely filter removal (ALL has a secondary use as a table function returning all rows).
